name: Zeno (of Elea)
biography: Mentioned as the disciple of Parmenides who, according to Russell, seems to have first practised dialectic systematically (as dramatized in Plato's Parmenides), suggesting Socrates developed rather than invented the method. His argument of the arrow (that the arrow, being at each instant simply where it is, is therefore always at rest) is used by Russell to expose the assumption shared by Zeno and Bergson -- that motion requires an internal 'state of motion' at each instant -- and to show that the mathematical account of continuous motion escapes the paradox while Bergson's account does not.
